standard_prerequisites.name: The completion of a discrete valuation ring is again a discrete valuation ring, in particular a domain
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the completed ring a complete local domain of dimension one, which is the setting the argument is carried out in.

standard_prerequisites.name: Krasner's lemma: a polynomial with a simple root survives a sufficiently small perturbation of its coefficients, the new root being close to the old one in the maximal-adic topology
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces a root beta in B of the approximating polynomial P_1 and allows beta to be chosen so that theta - beta lies in pi B.

standard_prerequisites.name: Nakayama's lemma applied to the finite module B over a complete local domain, and the equality of degrees making a surjective map between the two quotients an isomorphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the comparison map from A-completion[t] over P_1 to B is surjective and hence an isomorphism, which identifies the base change of L with M.

core_obligations: Record that the completion of A is again a discrete valuation ring and hence a domain, and announce that the argument works more generally for a Noetherian local ring whose completion is a local domain of dimension one (proof lines 33823-33827).

Choose a primitive element theta generating M over the completion of K, let P be its minimal polynomial, and clear denominators by replacing theta with a suitable multiple by a power of a nonzero element pi so that the coefficients of P lie in the completion of A (proof lines 33829-33835).

Set B equal to the quotient of the completed polynomial ring by P; note that B is a complete local domain of dimension one because it is finite over A and contained in M, and that separability ensures theta is not a root of the derivative of P (proof lines 33836-33839).

Approximate the polynomial: for every n find a monic P_1 in A[t] with P - P_1 having coefficients in pi^n times the completed polynomial ring, apply Krasner's lemma to get a root beta of P_1 in B for large n, and arrange theta - beta in pi B (proof lines 33839-33844).

Consider the map from the quotient of the completed polynomial ring by P_1 to B sending t to beta, observe that B equals pi B plus the span of the powers of theta below the degree of P, conclude surjectivity by Nakayama and hence an isomorphism by equality of degrees, and finish by setting L equal to K[t] over P_1; then the base change of L is M, so L is a field (proof lines 33844-33851).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a complete local domain of dimension one and choose a primitive element with minimal polynomial having coefficients in the completed ring (proof lines 33823-33835).
Form the finite complete local algebra B and use separability of theta to know the derivative does not vanish at it (proof lines 33836-33839).
Approximate the minimal polynomial by a monic polynomial over A, apply Krasner to obtain a root beta in B close to theta (proof lines 33839-33844).
Compare the two finite quotients by a Nakayama argument to get an isomorphism, read off the extension L over K whose base change is M and conclude that L is a field (proof lines 33844-33851).
difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K and completion, every finite separable extension of the completed fraction field arises by base change from a finite separable extension of K (statement lines 33813-33820). The proof combines three ingredients in one construction: a primitive element whose minimal polynomial is cleared into the completed ring, an approximation of that polynomial by a polynomial over A to within an arbitrarily high power of the maximal ideal, and Krasner's lemma, which turns the approximation into a root of the approximating polynomial inside the finite complete local algebra B, after which a Nakayama argument identifies the two quotients and the extension over K is read off (proof lines 33829-33851). The hypothesis of separability is used exactly where it is needed, namely to know that theta is not a root of the derivative so that Krasner applies. The counted span refers three times to earlier lemmas of this chapter, carried as navigation stubs.
